samples.summary: `isPaintableImageSize` drops (not clamps) any image whose stored height exceeds 20000 px, but no insert path bounds image height — a tall narrow image silently disappears on the next read
samples.evidence: `isPaintableImageSize` requires `height <= MAX_IMAGE_SIZE (20000)` and both CRDT readers (`crdt-tree.ts:99`, `yorkie-doc-store.ts:219`) now drop the whole `image` object when it fails, so the inline degrades to a bare U+FFFC with no picture. The only sizing guard on insert is `clampImageToWidth` (`packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:465`), which returns the input unchanged when `width <= maxWidth` and never touches `height`: `if (width <= maxWidth || width <= 0 || maxWidth <= 0) return { width, height };`. `editor.ts:4262` is the only clamp applied on `insertImage`. So a 600×25000 px long-page screenshot (width already under the ~624 px content width) is stored verbatim, renders locally, and is then dropped for every reader — including the author after reload — with no error. Dropping rather than clamping is the deliberate choice documented in the module header, which makes this silent content loss rather than a distorted image.

samples.summary: The dirty-marking added for carried children uses `doc.blockParentMap`, the exact stale/missing map the rest of the change routes around — a cell child absent from it marks a non-top-level id and the table repaints at the old indent
samples.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` does `const cellInfo = doc.blockParentMap.get(change.block.id); markDirty(cellInfo?.tableBlockId ?? change.block.id);`. `Doc.siblingBlocksOf` (document.ts:311) and the surrounding comments explicitly treat a parent-map miss as an ordinary state (a block created since the last layout pass, e.g. the tail block a paste splits out inside a cell). In that case `markDirty` is handed the child's own id, which is not a top-level block, so the containing table is never marked dirty and — since `indent()`/`outdent()` deliberately do not call `invalidateLayout()` (editor.ts:3624, 3647) — the cell's cached lines survive and repaint at the pre-change indent. The new test at test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts ('a cell caret missing from the parent map still carries its subtree') asserts only the model levels, not the painted x, so it cannot see this.

samples.summary: Outdenting a selection whose first list item is already at level 0 is now refused for the entire selection, including deeper items that previously outdented
samples.evidence: `planSiblingGroup` computes `subtreeOf(blocks, i)` for the first selected item, marks every member `covered`, and only then applies `if (delta < 0 && level <= 0) continue;`. For the common gesture 'select the whole list, press Shift+Tab' over `[a(0), b(1), c(1)]`, the level-0 root's subtree covers b and c, the root refuses, and the covered children are skipped — the gesture becomes a total no-op where the previous per-item code moved b and c to 0. The new test 'floor: a level-0 root refuses, and its children stay put' pins this, so it is intentional, but it is a user-visible regression on a normal-use path (select-all + outdent), not only on the parent/child pair the issue describes.

samples.summary: `paginatableRowHeight` clamps only the height pagination consumes; `LayoutTable.rowHeights`, `rowYOffsets` and `totalHeight` stay raw, so a clamped or NaN row leaves pagination and rendering/hit-testing disagreeing
samples.evidence: `const rowHeight = paginatableRowHeight(tl.rowHeights[ri], contentHeight);` feeds `currentY += rowHeight` and `rowLine.height`, but `rowLine.y = tl.rowYOffsets[ri]` and every downstream consumer (`getTableOriginYForPageLine`, row hit-testing, the scroll extent derived from `layout.totalHeight`) still reads the unclamped `LayoutTable` values. A NaN row height maps to 0 here, so the row is placed with zero advance while the renderer draws it at its NaN/huge geometry, and the rows that follow on the same page are laid at y positions that overlap it. Bounded-blast (only fires on out-of-band geometry that the CRDT bands mostly exclude), but the two halves of the fix are not kept consistent.

samples.summary: The new `lineHeight` band breaks the documented `GET` → `PUT` identity the same function's doc comment asserts: the v1 write validator accepts any finite lineHeight, which the reader now drops or clamps
samples.evidence: The doc comment above `parseBlockStyleAttrs` states 'This also keeps the v1 REST endpoint's `GET` → `PUT` identity intact, since the validator on the write side rejects exactly the values dropped here.' The write-side validator is `packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:399-407`, which for every `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` entry only rejects non-numbers and non-finite values. A `PUT` with `style.lineHeight: 0`, `-2` or `50` is therefore accepted and stored, but the reader added here deletes it (0, -2) or clamps it to 20 (50), so a subsequent `GET` no longer round-trips the body that was accepted. Either the validator needs the matching band or the comment's invariant no longer holds.

samples.summary: The clipboard paste path bypasses every new numeric band (fontSize, cell padding, rowHeights), so pasted out-of-band values enter the model unbanded and diverge from what the CRDT reader gives every other reader
samples.evidence: `clipboard.ts:211` does `const fontSize = asNumber(value.fontSize); if (fontSize !== undefined) marker.fontSize = fontSize;` — `asNumber` only checks finiteness, with no `normalizeFontSize` call, and the same is true of the pasted cell `padding` and `sanitizeTableData`'s `rowHeights` (which `table-layout.ts:252` acknowledges: 'the paste path (`sanitizeTableData`) admits any finite number'). A pasted `fontSize: 1e9` therefore lives in the local `Doc` at 1e9, is serialized to the CRDT, and comes back as 400 on the next read — the pasting client and every other client render the same document differently until reload. `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` was moved into the shared module for exactly this consistency reason; the other three bands were not applied here.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. `isPaintableImageSize` (numeric-attrs.ts:102-111) requires height <= MAX_IMAGE_SIZE=20000 (line 54), and both readers drop the entire image object when it fails (crdt-tree.ts:97-105, yorkie-doc-store.ts:217-227), leaving a bare U+FFFC. The only insert-time sizing guard is `clampImageToWidth` (types.ts:465-478), which returns the input unchanged when `width <= maxWidth` and never bounds absolute height; it is applied once at editor.ts:4262. Insert callers pass raw intrinsic dimensions with no ceiling (image-insert.ts:135-142, 180-184; loaders at 67-82 and 96-116 only reject zero). The write path persists height verbatim (yorkie-doc-store.ts:149, backend docs-tree.ts:99), and layout.ts:726-733 only scales when width exceeds the content width, so a narrow tall image renders correctly locally and then vanishes for every reader including the author after reload. The only height clamp that exists is on the resize gesture (image-selection-overlay.ts:596-597), which does not cover insert. Reachable with a real artifact (a >32:1 aspect-ratio long-page screenshot under ~624 px wide), silent, and unrecoverable since the choice is drop-not-clamp — content loss, in the correctness lane.
